spec_used: specs/aqa/science-8464-8464.md (cross-checked against specs/aqa/chemistry-8462-8462.md for the separate-science lessons)

findings.claim: "Both appear in the AQA required practicals" and "AQA's required practical investigates..."
findings.truth: House rule: student-facing text never names the exam board. Say "the required practicals".
findings.evidence: house style rule; the same page never names a board elsewhere

findings.claim: the required practical investigates "how changing one factor (e.g. concentration of acid or size of marble chips)"
findings.truth: The rates required practical investigates how changes in CONCENTRATION affect rate, by a gas-volume method and by a colour-change / turbidity method. Chip size is not the variable of the required practical.

findings.claim: extended-response mark scheme lists "Different reactions need specific catalysts, e.g. iron in the Haber process"
findings.truth: The Haber process is not in the combined spec, and the spec says students need not know catalyst names beyond those in the subject content. Harmless as one of nine indicative points, so not edited.
findings.evidence: spec 5.6.1.4; no Haber content anywhere in 8464

findings.claim: the mean-rate sentence and the "draw a tangent" paragraph sit inside the Higher-only block, which is hidden from Foundation users
findings.truth: Only CALCULATING the gradient of a tangent is Higher only; drawing a tangent and mean rate are examined at both tiers. The mean-rate equation is already given outside the block, so no content is actually lost. Left alone rather than restructure the block.

findings.claim: collapsible headed "Required Practical: Testing for Water"
findings.truth: Testing for water is not a required practical. The chemistry required practicals for this course are salt preparation, electrolysis, temperature changes, rates, chromatography and water analysis (numbers 8-13 of the 21 in this course; the 1-8 numbering belongs to the separate sciences).

findings.claim: cards 4 and 5 both have the answer "⇌"; their questions are fragments ("We show this using the equilibrium symbol _____", "Key Fact The _____ symbol tells you a reaction is reversible")
findings.truth: Two cards in one deck must not share an answer, and a cloze answer needs a question that stands on its own. Card 4 becomes a proper question for the symbol; card 5 becomes a dynamic-equilibrium card.

findings.claim: a full section on the Haber process (conditions, 450 degC, 200 atm, iron catalyst), a 4-mark practice question on it, and an exam tip telling students to use it in extended answers
findings.truth: The Haber process is separate-chemistry content and appears nowhere in the combined spec. Options: (a) delete the Haber section, its practice question and the exam-tip sentence, and replace the practice question with a general equilibrium question; (b) keep it, flagged as extension only. Recommendation: (a), and note that the Le Chatelier block above it is correctly flagged Higher only.
findings.evidence: 8464 has no Haber content; it is 4.10.4.1 of the separate chemistry spec

findings.claim: "Calculate the R₆ value of the dye", "R₆ = 24 ÷ 60", "comparing R₆ values"
findings.truth: The symbol is Rf (subscript f), not subscript 6. The arithmetic itself is right: 24 ÷ 60 = 0.40.

findings.claim: "Use pencil, not pen, because pencil ink is insoluble"
findings.truth: A pencil contains graphite, not ink. Say "pencil marks".

findings.claim: card 5 is "_____ atmospheric oxygen reached today's level of approximately 21%" with the answer "Eventually"; card 4 is a sentence fragment answered "Mars"
findings.truth: A card must test science, not a filler adverb, and a cloze stem must read as a question. Card 4 becomes a "Which planet..." question; card 5 becomes a greenhouse-effect card.

findings.claim: "The four atmospheric pollutants you must know for AQA are..." and the matching revision tip "...the 4 atmospheric pollutants for AQA"
findings.truth: House rule: student-facing text never names the exam board.

findings.claim: card answers "C8345H83228345" and "C8322H8324"
findings.truth: Mangled numeric character references: they should read CₙH₂ₙ and C₂H₄. Both stems were also fragments, so both are rewritten as questions.

findings.claim: description is exactly 100 characters
findings.truth: The limit is under 100 characters, so the row sits on the validator edge. Shortened.

findings.claim: a whole lesson on addition reactions of alkenes, alcohols, carboxylic acids and esters, taught as examined content
findings.truth: None of this is in the combined spec: topic 5.7 for this course is only 5.7.1 (crude oil, alkanes, fractional distillation, properties, cracking). Alcohols, carboxylic acids and esters are separate-chemistry content (4.7.2). The lesson slug is lesson-04 and its diagram is served from separate-sciences/chemistry-separate, so it looks like a copy of a separate-science lesson. Options: (a) unpublish lessons 8-11 from this combined unit; (b) keep them, clearly badged as extension work that is not examined on this course. Recommendation: (a); Unity teaches separate sciences in its own subject row, and combined students should not revise it.

findings.claim: the Higher-only wrapper covers "What Are Polymers?" and "Addition Polymerisation", while condensation polymerisation and amino acids sit outside it
findings.truth: It is the wrong way round. Addition polymerisation, and the definitions of polymer and monomer, are examined at both tiers; condensation polymerisation and amino acids are Higher only; DNA and the other natural polymers are both tiers. Foundation users currently lose the core half and see the Higher half. Wrapper moved.
findings.evidence: chemistry-8462 4.7.3.1 (no flag), 4.7.3.2 (HT only), 4.7.3.3 (HT only), 4.7.3.4 (no flag); css/style.css hides .higher-only for Foundation

findings.claim: card 4 reads "_____ (C₂H₄) is the monomer"
findings.truth: A cloze stem must read as a question; rewritten as "Which alkene is the monomer used to make poly(ethene)?"

findings.claim: a whole lesson on addition and condensation polymerisation, amino acids, proteins, starch and DNA
findings.truth: Not in the combined spec. Polymers appear in this course only in topic 5.2.2.5 (large molecules, strong covalent bonds, solids at room temperature), which is Chemistry Paper 1 content. Same options as F14; recommendation: unpublish from this unit.
findings.evidence: spec 5.2.2.5 and 5.7.1; the whole of 5.7.2 is absent from 8464

findings.claim: "Lithium (Li¹⁺)", "Sodium (Na¹⁺)", "Potassium (K¹⁺)"
findings.truth: A single positive charge is written as +, not 1+. The ions are Li⁺, Na⁺ and K⁺.

findings.claim: card 4 is "_____ Test Colours in Detail Lithium (Li¹⁺): Produces a crimson (deep red) flame" answered "Flame"; card 5 is "_____ (Na¹⁺): Produces a strong yellow flame"
findings.truth: Both were scraped from headings. Rewritten as flame-colour questions answered "Lithium" and "Sodium".

findings.claim: a whole lesson on flame tests, sodium hydroxide precipitates, halide and sulfate tests and flame emission spectroscopy
findings.truth: Not in the combined spec. Chemical analysis for this course is purity, formulations, chromatography and the four gas tests only (5.8.1 and 5.8.2); identification of metal ions and instrumental analysis are separate-chemistry content (4.8.3). Every fact in the lesson checked out, so this is purely a scope call. Same options as F14; recommendation: unpublish from this unit.

findings.claim: "Concrete: Gravel or crusite (reinforcement) held together by cement (matrix)"
findings.truth: "Crusite" is not a material. Concrete is gravel or crushed stone in a cement matrix.

findings.claim: a whole lesson on corrosion, alloys, ceramics and composites, the Haber process and NPK fertilisers
findings.truth: None of it is in the combined spec: 5.10 for this course stops at potable water, waste water, low-grade ore extraction (Higher only), life cycle assessment and reducing resource use. Alloys are in this course, but in topic 5.2.2.7, which sits on Chemistry Paper 1, not Paper 2. Two further points if the lesson is kept: the equilibrium reasoning about temperature and pressure ("shifts the equilibrium towards the side with fewer gas molecules") is Higher-only content sitting outside the Higher flag, and the figures checked out (450 degC, 200 atm, iron catalyst, about 15% yield; 12/80 = 15%). Same options as F14; recommendation: unpublish from this unit.
findings.evidence: spec 5.10 contents and 5.2.2.7; chemistry-8462 4.10.3, 4.10.4 (both marked chemistry only)

summary: Every equation balances and every calculation recomputes correctly across the 11 lessons (rates 45/90 = 0.5 cm3/s, Rf 24/60 = 0.40 and 30/52 = 0.58, decane 120/142 = 84.5%, 12500 x 0.185 = 2.3125 t, particulates 18/45 = 40%, aluminium 170 x 0.95 = 161.5 GJ, 1000 monomers give 999 water molecules, 12/80 = 15%), all 55 knowledge-check answer keys are right, and the paper structure claims match the spec. The real damage is elsewhere: four lessons (8-11) are separate-science lessons sitting in a combined unit and are flagged ADJUDICATE rather than edited away; five flashcard decks carry scraped or mangled cards, including mangled entities and a duplicated answer; the Higher flag in lesson 9 is on the wrong half of the lesson; and the exam board is named in student-facing text in two lessons.
